overview: 48 official Qs (2008, 2017, 2019, 2025). Three clusters: unitary vs federal features (13), elections and electoral reforms (13) and Centre-State relations – Art 356, Inter-State/Zonal Councils (11); commissions (Rajamannar, Sarkaria, Punchhi) 5; parties and recognition 5. One-liners on 'who said / which Article / which year', many negative stems, and 2025 assertion-reason, matching and chronology.

possibility.angle: Centre-State relations: Art 356, Inter-State and Zonal Councils, AP episodes
possibility.what_they_ask: Art 356 and S.R. Bommai; Inter-State Council (Art 263, consensus, 1990); Zonal Councils (States Reorganisation Act 1956, Union Home Minister chairs); AP President's Rule 1973; Governor Ram Lal and NTR (1984); AIS as anti-federal.
which committee is (not) on Centre-State relations – odd one out among commissions.
set up by Tamil Nadu (1969) to study Centre-State relations; recommendations – Inter-State Council, curb Art 356, abolish IAS/IPS (not strengthen Governor).
Governor criteria – eminent, outsider to the State, detached from local politics, secure 5-year term.
2007 (UPA); fixed 5-year Governor tenure; amend Arts 355/356 for localised emergency.

who described India how (Wheare quasi-federal, Jennings centralising, Ambedkar unitary-and-federal); which is not a federal feature (CAG); Art 1 'Union of States'; Art 3 – views of State not binding; Schedule I for new State; Emergency grounds and consequences.
TDP largest opposition party 1984; chronology of party founding (DMK 1949 → TDP 1982 → BSP 1984 → SP 1992); media and political image.
natural targets: one-party dominance ('Congress system', Rajni Kothari), multi-party coalition era from 1989, regional parties' rise – likely in the same 'who described / which year' style.

possibility.angle: Recognition of national and State parties
possibility.what_they_ask: Symbols Order 1968 criteria (6% votes in 4 States + 4 LS seats; 2% LS seats from 3 States; State party in 4 States); which party is national (names with 'All India' mislead).

NOTA 2013; National Voters' Day 25 Jan; EVM history (Paravur 1982, 1998 trial in Rajasthan/MP/Delhi, Goa 1999); 61st Amd voting age 18; MCC voluntary; committees (Vohra, Indrajit Gupta, Dinesh Goswami); Sangha seat; mid-term vs by-election; Art 192 disqualification to Governor.
natural targets: 52nd Amd 1985 (Tenth Schedule), 91st Amd 2003 (split clause removed, merger needs 2/3), Speaker/Chairman decides, Kihoto Hollohan (1992) judicial review.

traps.trap: Swaps the author of a description of Indian federalism [Wheare / Jennings / Ambedkar]
traps.spot: 'Who described India as ...' with constitutional experts as options
traps.fix: Wheare – quasi-federal; Ivor Jennings – federation with a strong centralising tendency; Ambedkar – unitary or federal as time and circumstances require; Austin – cooperative federalism; Morris-Jones – bargaining federalism.
traps.pyq: 'Quasi-federal' → K.C. Wheare [group2-2008-paper2#147]; 'federation with a centralising tendency' → Ivor Jennings, not Wheare [mains-2025-paper1#99]

traps.trap: Turns a consultative step into a binding one
traps.fix: President refers the bill to the State legislature for its VIEWS – Parliament is not bound.
traps.pyq: Altering boundary of a State → views of the affected State Assembly are to be sought by the President [prelims-2017#34]

traps.trap: Revives a pre-1978 Emergency ground or power
traps.spot: Grounds of Art 352, or 'suspend all FRs'
traps.fix: Grounds now: war, external aggression, armed rebellion ('internal disturbance' removed by the 44th Amd). Arts 20 and 21 can never be suspended.
traps.pyq: Cannot proclaim on 'Internal Disturbance' [prelims-2019#65]; 'suspend all the Fundamental Rights' → false consequence [mains-2025-paper1#114]

traps.trap: Gives a statutory council constitutional status
traps.fix: Inter-State Council – Art 263 (constitutional). Zonal Councils – States Reorganisation Act 1956; river water tribunals – 1956 Act under Art 262 (statutory).
traps.pyq: Constitutional body → Inter State Council [mains-2017-paper2#146]; Zonal Councils → States Reorganisation Act 1956 [group2-2008-paper2#144]

traps.trap: Plants a recommendation the commission never made (often the opposite)
traps.fix: Rajamannar wanted State autonomy – so 'strengthening the Governor' is foreign to it. Punchhi wanted Arts 355/356 amended (localised emergency).
traps.pyq: 'Strengthening of Governor System' → not Rajamannar [mains-2017-paper2#135]; 'no need to amend Article 355 and 356' → wrong about Punchhi [mains-2017-paper2#131]

traps.trap: Mixes up the committee with its electoral subject
traps.spot: Matching of committees and reforms; odd-one-out among commissions
traps.fix: Vohra – crime-politics nexus; Indrajit Gupta – State funding of elections; Dinesh Goswami – electoral reforms; J.S. Verma (2013) – criminal law.
traps.pyq: Indrajit Gupta Committee → not on Centre-State relations [mains-2025-paper1#116]; Vohra → crime-politics, Indrajit Gupta → State funding [mains-2025-paper1#95]

traps.trap: Swaps the place or year of an EVM 'first'
traps.spot: Statements on first use of EVMs
traps.fix: First ever: Paravur (Kerala) 1982; experimental 1998 in 16 constituencies of Rajasthan, MP, Delhi; first whole State: Goa 1999.
traps.pyq: Statement B on 1998 trial with wrong States → not true; Goa 1999 → true [mains-2025-paper1#93]

traps.trap: Takes the name of a party as proof of national status
traps.spot: 'All India' or 'of India' in party names
traps.fix: Recognition depends on Symbols Order criteria, not the name; AIFB, PWPI, RSP, DMK were State parties in 2019.
traps.pyq: None of DMK, RSP, AIFB, PWPI is national → None of these [mains-2019-paper2#128]

techniques.name: Federal-feature filter [divides power vs centralises]
techniques.how: Ask of each option: does it divide power between two levels and protect that division (written, rigid, supreme Constitution, independent judiciary, division of powers)? Single integrated institutions (CAG, Governor, AIS, Emergency) are unitary.
techniques.example: Rigid Constitution, distribution of powers, independent SC are federal; CAG audits both levels as one office → not federal [mains-2017-paper2#126]; Governor, CAG, Emergency violate federal principle, Central Services do not → A, C and D [mains-2025-paper1#103]

techniques.name: Chronology by founding anchors
techniques.how: Pin each party to a known event: DMK 1949 (Annadurai split from DK), TDP 1982 (NTR), BSP 1984 (Kanshi Ram), SP 1992 (Mulayam). Fix the earliest and latest first.
techniques.example: DMK earliest, SP latest → only options starting B and ending A survive → TDP 1982 before BSP 1984 → B, D, C, A [mains-2025-paper1#101]

techniques.name: Assertion-reason: can a later event explain an earlier text?
techniques.how: If R is a later recommendation and A is an original constitutional provision, R cannot be its explanation even if both are true.
techniques.example: Art 263 (1950) vs Rajamannar's 1969 case for an Inter-State Council → both true, R not the explanation [mains-2025-paper1#113]

techniques.name: Whose desk? routing
techniques.how: For disqualification and dispute questions, route by office: MP disqualification → President on ECI opinion (Art 103); MLA → Governor on ECI opinion (Art 192); defection → Speaker/Chairman.
techniques.example: Art 192 disqualification of an MLA is referred to → Governor of the State [mains-2017-paper2#121]

techniques.name: Commission-intent check
techniques.how: Recall each body's purpose (Rajamannar = more State autonomy; Sarkaria/Punchhi = balanced Governor reforms). A recommendation against that purpose is the odd one.
techniques.example: Sarkaria wanted an eminent outsider with a secure term; 'should have travelled extensively in the State' is no criterion → answer [mains-2017-paper2#144]

confusions.remember: Wheare = quasi-federal; Jennings = federation with a centralising tendency.
Austin = cooperative federalism; Morris-Jones = bargaining federalism.
Constitutional vs statutory; ISC decides by consensus; ZCs chaired by Union Home Minister.
Rajamannar: State autonomy, abolish AIS; Sarkaria: balanced reforms, ISC set up 1990.
Punchhi: fixed 5-year Governor tenure, removal by State legislature resolution, localised emergency.
356 State machinery failure; 352 National Emergency; 360 Financial Emergency; 358 suspends Art 19.
New States by ordinary law amending Schedule I; not an Art 368 amendment.
Mid-term = whole House dissolved early; by-election = one vacant seat.
Gupta – State funding; Goswami – electoral reforms; Vohra – criminal-politics nexus.
First EVM use anywhere vs first entire State election by EVM.
Art 326 age change vs Tenth Schedule.
Dismissal by Ram Lal; reinstatement under his successor.

anchors: Art 1 – 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'
Art 3 – new States by law; Schedule I amended
Art 263 – Inter-State Council (set up 1990, decisions by consensus)
Art 352 grounds: war, external aggression, armed rebellion (44th Amd)
Art 353 – directions to any State in Emergency; Art 354 – finance modified
Art 192 – MLA disqualification to Governor on ECI opinion
NOTA – PUCL 2013; National Voters' Day 25 Jan
EVM: Paravur 1982; Goa 1999 first whole State
MCC – no statutory backing, consensus of parties
TDP 1984 – largest opposition party in Lok Sabha (30 seats)
checklist: Quote question: Wheare, Jennings, Ambedkar, Austin – whose phrase exactly?
Federal-feature question: does the option divide power or concentrate it?
Constitutional or statutory body? Look for an Article.
Emergency: is the option a post-1978 ground or power?
Commission: does the option fit the commission's purpose?
Election firsts: place, year and scale (constituency / whole State).
